question.text: What are pavement markings, and what do yellow centerlines separate?

answer.text: Pavement markings are lines, words or figures placed on the pavement with paint, reflectors or other markers, and yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

teaching.text: Pavement markings are lines, words or figures placed on the pavement with paint, reflectors or other markers, and yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. This matters because yellow means opposing traffic is on the other side; white means same-direction traffic. Remember: Yellow splits opposite directions. Once more, Yellow splits opposite directions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Pavement markings are lines, words or figures placed on the pavement with paint, reflectors or other markers, and yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question.text: What does a single broken yellow centerline mean?

answer.text: A single broken yellow centerline marks a road with only two lanes of traffic, you drive to its right, and you may cross it to pass another vehicle when it is safe.

teaching.text: A single broken yellow centerline marks a road with only two lanes of traffic, you drive to its right, and you may cross it to pass another vehicle when it is safe. Remember: Broken yellow, pass when safe. Once more, Broken yellow, pass when safe.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A single broken yellow centerline marks a road with only two lanes of traffic, you drive to its right, and you may cross it to pass another vehicle when it is safe.

question.text: What do double solid yellow lines mean, and when may you cross them?

answer.text: Double solid yellow lines mark the center of a road where passing is prohibited in both directions, and you may cross them only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road or driveway.

teaching.text: Double solid yellow lines mark the center of a road where passing is prohibited in both directions, and you may cross them only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road or driveway. Remember: Double yellow, left turns only. Once more, Double yellow, left turns only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Double solid yellow lines mark the center of a road where passing is prohibited in both directions, and you may cross them only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road or driveway.

question.text: What is a no passing line, and when may you cross it?

answer.text: A no passing line is a single solid yellow line on a two-lane road marking a zone where passing is prohibited, and like the double yellow line it may be crossed only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road or driveway.

teaching.text: A no passing line is a single solid yellow line on a two-lane road marking a zone where passing is prohibited, and like the double yellow line it may be crossed only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road or driveway. This matters because the left-turn exception applies to both the single and the double solid yellow line. Remember: Solid yellow, driveway turns only. Once more, Solid yellow, driveway turns only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A no passing line is a single solid yellow line on a two-lane road marking a zone where passing is prohibited, and like the double yellow line it may be crossed only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road or driveway.

question.text: How does a broken yellow centerline differ from a solid no passing line?

answer.text: A broken yellow centerline may be crossed to pass when safe, while a solid yellow no passing line may be crossed only for a left turn into or out of an alley, private road or driveway.

teaching.text: A broken yellow centerline may be crossed to pass when safe, while a solid yellow no passing line may be crossed only for a left turn into or out of an alley, private road or driveway. Remember: Broken pass, solid turn only. Once more, Broken pass, solid turn only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A broken yellow centerline may be crossed to pass when safe, while a solid yellow no passing line may be crossed only for a left turn into or out of an alley, private road or driveway.

question.text: How do yellow lines differ from white lines?

answer.text: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, while white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

teaching.text: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, while white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Remember: Yellow opposite, white same. Once more, Yellow opposite, white same.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, while white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

recap.narration_text: Quick recap of yellow line rules and the left-turn exception. Yellow splits opposite directions. Broken yellow, pass when safe. Double yellow, left turns only. Solid yellow, driveway turns only. Broken pass, solid turn only. Yellow opposite, white same. That is the recap.

question.text: What do white lines separate?

answer.text: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and you are required to drive between them.

teaching.text: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and you are required to drive between them. Remember: White splits same direction. Once more, White splits same direction.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and you are required to drive between them.

question.text: When may you cross a single dashed white lane line?

answer.text: A single dashed white lane line may be crossed whenever you can do so safely.

teaching.text: A single dashed white lane line may be crossed whenever you can do so safely. Remember: Dashed white, cross when safe. Once more, Dashed white, cross when safe.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A single dashed white lane line may be crossed whenever you can do so safely.

question.text: What does a single solid white line mean?

answer.text: A single solid white line warns that changing lanes there is hazardous, a wider line signals a greater hazard, and such a line may be crossed only in unusual circumstances and only with great care.

teaching.text: A single solid white line warns that changing lanes there is hazardous, a wider line signals a greater hazard, and such a line may be crossed only in unusual circumstances and only with great care. Remember: Solid white, hazardous change. Once more, Solid white, hazardous change.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A single solid white line warns that changing lanes there is hazardous, a wider line signals a greater hazard, and such a line may be crossed only in unusual circumstances and only with great care.

question.text: What does a double solid white line mean?

answer.text: A double solid white line means that moving from lane to lane is prohibited, and you must not cross it.

teaching.text: A double solid white line means that moving from lane to lane is prohibited, and you must not cross it. This matters because single solid white may be crossed with great care; double solid white may never be crossed. Remember: Double white, never cross. Once more, Double white, never cross.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A double solid white line means that moving from lane to lane is prohibited, and you must not cross it.

question.text: How does a single solid white line differ from a double solid white?

answer.text: A single solid white line may be crossed only in unusual circumstances with great care, while a double solid white line may never be crossed.

teaching.text: A single solid white line may be crossed only in unusual circumstances with great care, while a double solid white line may never be crossed. Remember: Single rare, double never. Once more, Single rare, double never.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A single solid white line may be crossed only in unusual circumstances with great care, while a double solid white line may never be crossed.

recap.narration_text: Quick recap of white lane line rules. White splits same direction. Dashed white, cross when safe. Solid white, hazardous change. Double white, never cross. Single rare, double never. That is the recap.

question.text: What are obstruction markings?

answer.text: Obstruction markings are solid lines in the traffic lanes, yellow or white, that steer you around an obstruction in the road such as a bridge support.

teaching.text: Obstruction markings are solid lines in the traffic lanes, yellow or white, that steer you around an obstruction in the road such as a bridge support. Remember: Solid lines steer around obstruction. Once more, Solid lines steer around obstruction.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Obstruction markings are solid lines in the traffic lanes, yellow or white, that steer you around an obstruction in the road such as a bridge support.

question.text: How do white and yellow obstruction markings differ in passing?

answer.text: White obstruction markings may be passed on either side, but yellow obstruction markings must be kept on your left, so you pass them on the right only.

teaching.text: White obstruction markings may be passed on either side, but yellow obstruction markings must be kept on your left, so you pass them on the right only. This matters because yellow keeps you to the right because opposing traffic is on the other side of it. Remember: White either side, yellow right. Once more, White either side, yellow right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: White obstruction markings may be passed on either side, but yellow obstruction markings must be kept on your left, so you pass them on the right only.

question.text: What do directional arrows and words in the lane require?

answer.text: Directional markings are white arrows or words painted in the lane to show the direction you must take, you must move only as the arrow indicates, and where arrows show more than one direction you may choose any of them.

teaching.text: Directional markings are white arrows or words painted in the lane to show the direction you must take, you must move only as the arrow indicates, and where arrows show more than one direction you may choose any of them. Remember: Follow arrow, several means choice. Once more, Follow arrow, several means choice.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Directional markings are white arrows or words painted in the lane to show the direction you must take, you must move only as the arrow indicates, and where arrows show more than one direction you may choose any of them.

question.text: How do you pass white versus yellow obstruction markings?

answer.text: White obstruction markings may be passed on either side, while yellow obstruction markings must be passed on the right only.

teaching.text: White obstruction markings may be passed on either side, while yellow obstruction markings must be passed on the right only. Remember: White either, yellow right only. Once more, White either, yellow right only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: White obstruction markings may be passed on either side, while yellow obstruction markings must be passed on the right only.

question.text: How does a single arrow differ from a lane with several arrows?

answer.text: A single directional arrow commands one movement only, while a lane with arrows for more than one direction lets you choose any of those directions.

teaching.text: A single directional arrow commands one movement only, while a lane with arrows for more than one direction lets you choose any of those directions. Remember: One arrow commands, several choose. Once more, One arrow commands, several choose.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A single directional arrow commands one movement only, while a lane with arrows for more than one direction lets you choose any of those directions.

recap.narration_text: Quick recap of obstruction and directional markings. Solid lines steer around obstruction. White either side, yellow right. Follow arrow, several means choice. White either, yellow right only. One arrow commands, several choose. That is the recap.

question.text: What is a two-way left turn lane, and what may it never be used for?

answer.text: Two-way left turn channelization markings combine solid and dashed yellow lines to mark a center lane that vehicles traveling in either direction may use only for left turns, and the lane must never be used for passing.

teaching.text: Two-way left turn channelization markings combine solid and dashed yellow lines to mark a center lane that vehicles traveling in either direction may use only for left turns, and the lane must never be used for passing. This matters because the shared center lane is for turning only, never for passing or through travel. Remember: Center lane turns, never passing. Once more, Center lane turns, never passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Two-way left turn channelization markings combine solid and dashed yellow lines to mark a center lane that vehicles traveling in either direction may use only for left turns, and the lane must never be used for passing.

question.text: What is a stop line?

answer.text: A stop line is a solid white line running across the lanes at an intersection or pedestrian crosswalk, and it shows exactly where to stop.

teaching.text: A stop line is a solid white line running across the lanes at an intersection or pedestrian crosswalk, and it shows exactly where to stop. Remember: Stop line shows exact stop. Once more, Stop line shows exact stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A stop line is a solid white line running across the lanes at an intersection or pedestrian crosswalk, and it shows exactly where to stop.

question.text: What do crosswalk lines mean for drivers?

answer.text: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to cross safely and warn drivers that pedestrians may be crossing at that spot, and you must stop for pedestrians in crosswalks.

teaching.text: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to cross safely and warn drivers that pedestrians may be crossing at that spot, and you must stop for pedestrians in crosswalks. Remember: Stop for crosswalk pedestrians. Once more, Stop for crosswalk pedestrians.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to cross safely and warn drivers that pedestrians may be crossing at that spot, and you must stop for pedestrians in crosswalks.

question.text: How does a two-way left turn lane differ from plain double yellow?

answer.text: The two-way left turn lane is open to vehicles from both directions for left turns only, while double solid yellow lines without such a lane allow crossing only for a left turn into a driveway or alley.

teaching.text: The two-way left turn lane is open to vehicles from both directions for left turns only, while double solid yellow lines without such a lane allow crossing only for a left turn into a driveway or alley. Remember: Turn lane both ways, yellow driveways. Once more, Turn lane both ways, yellow driveways.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The two-way left turn lane is open to vehicles from both directions for left turns only, while double solid yellow lines without such a lane allow crossing only for a left turn into a driveway or alley.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Turn lane both ways, yellow driveways

question.text: How does a stop line differ from crosswalk lines?

answer.text: A stop line marks the exact stopping place at an intersection or crosswalk, while crosswalk lines mark where pedestrians cross and oblige drivers to stop for them.

teaching.text: A stop line marks the exact stopping place at an intersection or crosswalk, while crosswalk lines mark where pedestrians cross and oblige drivers to stop for them. Remember: Line stops you, crosswalk protects. Once more, Line stops you, crosswalk protects.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A stop line marks the exact stopping place at an intersection or crosswalk, while crosswalk lines mark where pedestrians cross and oblige drivers to stop for them.

question.text: What do railroad crossing pavement markings consist of?

answer.text: Railroad crossing markings are white markings in the traffic lane before a crossing, consisting of a large X with two R letters, a solid yellow centerline running the whole distance to prevent passing, and a white stop line across the lane.

teaching.text: Railroad crossing markings are white markings in the traffic lane before a crossing, consisting of a large X with two R letters, a solid yellow centerline running the whole distance to prevent passing, and a white stop line across the lane. Remember: X, two R's, yellow line, stop. Once more, X, two R's, yellow line, stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Railroad crossing markings are white markings in the traffic lane before a crossing, consisting of a large X with two R letters, a solid yellow centerline running the whole distance to prevent passing, and a white stop line across the lane.

question.text: What are traffic islands, and what do they do?

answer.text: Traffic islands come in many designs, from painted markings alone to combinations of curbing, paving or landscaping, and they are used to direct you into separate traffic lanes.

teaching.text: Traffic islands come in many designs, from painted markings alone to combinations of curbing, paving or landscaping, and they are used to direct you into separate traffic lanes. Remember: Islands separate traffic lanes. Once more, Islands separate traffic lanes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Traffic islands come in many designs, from painted markings alone to combinations of curbing, paving or landscaping, and they are used to direct you into separate traffic lanes.

question.text: What is a safety island, and what must you never do with islands?

answer.text: A traffic island is called a safety island when it protects pedestrians who may have to stand in the roadway, and you should never drive into or across a traffic island.

teaching.text: A traffic island is called a safety island when it protects pedestrians who may have to stand in the roadway, and you should never drive into or across a traffic island. Remember: Safety island shelters, never cross. Once more, Safety island shelters, never cross.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A traffic island is called a safety island when it protects pedestrians who may have to stand in the roadway, and you should never drive into or across a traffic island.

question.text: How does a traffic island differ from a safety island?

answer.text: A traffic island directs vehicles into separate lanes, while a safety island is a traffic island that shelters pedestrians, and neither may be driven into or across.

teaching.text: A traffic island directs vehicles into separate lanes, while a safety island is a traffic island that shelters pedestrians, and neither may be driven into or across. Remember: Island splits lanes, safety shelters. Once more, Island splits lanes, safety shelters.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A traffic island directs vehicles into separate lanes, while a safety island is a traffic island that shelters pedestrians, and neither may be driven into or across.

question.text: How do railroad markings differ from red pavement markings?

answer.text: Railroad crossing pavement markings are white with a yellow no-passing centerline, while red pavement markings mean a roadway must not be entered at all.

teaching.text: Railroad crossing pavement markings are white with a yellow no-passing centerline, while red pavement markings mean a roadway must not be entered at all. Remember: Railroad white, red forbidden. Once more, Railroad white, red forbidden.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Railroad crossing pavement markings are white with a yellow no-passing centerline, while red pavement markings mean a roadway must not be entered at all.

question.text: What controls traffic flow, and what are the three categories of devices?

answer.text: Traffic flow is controlled by pavement markings, traffic islands, signals and signs, and these devices fall into three categories, regulatory devices, warning devices, and guide and information signs.

teaching.text: Traffic flow is controlled by pavement markings, traffic islands, signals and signs, and these devices fall into three categories, regulatory devices, warning devices, and guide and information signs. This matters because the three-category framework organizes the whole chapter. Remember: Regulatory, warning, guide. Once more, Regulatory, warning, guide.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Traffic flow is controlled by pavement markings, traffic islands, signals and signs, and these devices fall into three categories, regulatory devices, warning devices, and guide and information signs.

question.text: What do regulatory devices require, and what happens if you ignore them?

answer.text: Regulatory devices tell you to stop, to go a certain direction or to limit your speed, every regulatory device demands an action from you, and failing to comply is subject to penalty.

teaching.text: Regulatory devices tell you to stop, to go a certain direction or to limit your speed, every regulatory device demands an action from you, and failing to comply is subject to penalty. Remember: Regulatory demands action, penalty. Once more, Regulatory demands action, penalty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Regulatory devices tell you to stop, to go a certain direction or to limit your speed, every regulatory device demands an action from you, and failing to comply is subject to penalty.

question.text: What do warning devices do, and what risk comes from ignoring them?

answer.text: Warning devices advise you of hazardous conditions or the possibility of them, and ignoring a warning device can lead to a crash caused by your own negligence.

teaching.text: Warning devices advise you of hazardous conditions or the possibility of them, and ignoring a warning device can lead to a crash caused by your own negligence. Remember: Warning advises, ignoring crashes. Once more, Warning advises, ignoring crashes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Warning devices advise you of hazardous conditions or the possibility of them, and ignoring a warning device can lead to a crash caused by your own negligence.

question.text: What is the purpose of guide and information signs?

answer.text: Guide and information signs help you find your way safely or give information that makes the trip more comfortable.

teaching.text: Guide and information signs help you find your way safely or give information that makes the trip more comfortable. Remember: Find your way comfortably. Once more, Find your way comfortably.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Guide and information signs help you find your way safely or give information that makes the trip more comfortable.

question.text: What do red pavement markings or reflectors mean?

answer.text: Red pavement markings or red reflectors mark a roadway that must not be entered or used.

teaching.text: Red pavement markings or red reflectors mark a roadway that must not be entered or used. Remember: Red means do not enter. Once more, Red means do not enter.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Red pavement markings or red reflectors mark a roadway that must not be entered or used.

question.text: What are edge lines, and which colors go where?

answer.text: Edge lines are solid white or yellow lines along the edge of the roadway used as a safety guide, with white along the right edge and yellow allowed along the left edge of divided streets and highways.

teaching.text: Edge lines are solid white or yellow lines along the edge of the roadway used as a safety guide, with white along the right edge and yellow allowed along the left edge of divided streets and highways. Remember: White right edge, yellow left. Once more, White right edge, yellow left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Edge lines are solid white or yellow lines along the edge of the roadway used as a safety guide, with white along the right edge and yellow allowed along the left edge of divided streets and highways.

question.text: Which edge line color runs on which side?

answer.text: White edge lines run along the right edge of the roadway, while yellow edge lines may run along the left edge of a divided highway.

teaching.text: White edge lines run along the right edge of the roadway, while yellow edge lines may run along the left edge of a divided highway. Remember: White right, yellow left divided. Once more, White right, yellow left divided.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: White edge lines run along the right edge of the roadway, while yellow edge lines may run along the left edge of a divided highway.

question.text: How does a regulatory device differ from a warning device?

answer.text: A regulatory device requires an action and carries a penalty for non-compliance, while a warning device advises of a hazard and ignoring it risks a crash through negligence.

teaching.text: A regulatory device requires an action and carries a penalty for non-compliance, while a warning device advises of a hazard and ignoring it risks a crash through negligence. Remember: Regulatory penalty, warning crash. Once more, Regulatory penalty, warning crash.
